items.stem: Why build shell commands with a list of arguments to subprocess rather than one concatenated string with shell=True?

options.text: It avoids shell-injection and quoting bugs by passing arguments directly to the program
options.rationale: Correct: passing an argument list bypasses the shell, so untrusted values cannot inject commands.
Speed is not the reason; safety and correctness are.

options.text: It is the only way to capture output
options.rationale: Output capture works either way; the list form is about safety.
subprocess does not add retries; that is your logic.

items.explanation: Correct: passing an argument list bypasses the shell, so untrusted values cannot inject commands.

items.stem: Which practices make a CLI tool well-behaved in automation pipelines? (Select TWO)

options.text: Return a non-zero exit code on failure so callers can detect it
options.rationale: Correct: exit codes are how shells and scripts know whether a step succeeded.

options.text: Send diagnostics to logs/stderr and keep stdout for real output
options.rationale: Correct: separating diagnostics from results lets output be piped cleanly.

options.text: Always exit 0 so the pipeline never stops
options.rationale: Masking failures with exit 0 hides real errors from the pipeline.

options.text: Print progress bars into stdout that is being piped to a file
options.rationale: Progress noise in piped stdout corrupts the real output.

items.explanation: Correct: exit codes are how shells and scripts know whether a step succeeded.; Correct: separating diagnostics from results lets output be piped cleanly.

items.stem: What makes a batch file operation idempotent?

options.text: Running it again after a partial failure produces the same end state without duplicating work
options.rationale: Correct: idempotency means re-running converges on the same result, which makes retries safe.

options.text: It can only ever be run once
options.rationale: That is the opposite of idempotency.

options.text: It runs twice as fast the second time
It disables logging on the second run
options.rationale: Logging behaviour is unrelated to idempotency.

items.explanation: Correct: idempotency means re-running converges on the same result, which makes retries safe.
